stem: Let f(x) = sin(2x). What is the average rate of change of f on the interval [0, π/4]?

rationales.A: Dropped the coefficient inside the argument: using sin(π/4) - sin(0) = √2/2 instead of sin(2·π/4) - sin(0), then dividing by π/4, gives 2√2/π.
rationales.B: Average rate of change = (f(π/4) - f(0))/(π/4 - 0) = (sin(π/2) - sin(0))/(π/4) = (1 - 0)/(π/4) = 4/π.
rationales.C: Did not divide by the interval length: f(π/4) - f(0) = 1 - 0 = 1 is the change in f, not its average rate of change.
rationales.D: Sign reversed: computing (f(0) - f(π/4))/(π/4) = (0 - 1)/(π/4) gives -4/π. The earlier value must be subtracted from the later value.

misconception_map.A: Drops the coefficient inside the argument when evaluating, for example using the value at x instead of at kx
misconception_map.C: Gives the change in the function without dividing by the interval length
misconception_map.D: Subtracts in the wrong order, so the sign is reversed
